# Julia

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from julia/lang.json and julia/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check Julia code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- init --apply
```

For a Julia project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small Julia package from [`julia/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/julia/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//julia:defs.bzl", "julia_library", "julia_test")

julia_library(
    name = "Greet",
    srcs = ["src/Greet.jl"],
    data = ["Project.toml"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

julia_test(
    name = "Greet_test",
    size = "small",
    srcs = ["test/runtests.jl"],
    deps = [":Greet"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Dependencies

### Packages

Pin your packages in a `Manifest.bazel.json` and load it in `MODULE.bazel`:

```python
julia = use_extension("@rules_dx//julia:extensions.bzl", "julia")
julia.from_manifest(
    name = "app_pkgs",
    lockfile = "//:Manifest.bazel.json",
)
use_repo(julia, "app_pkgs")
```

## Generate

`dx generate` reads `Project.toml` only.

- A `Project.toml` with a `name` and a `src/<name>.jl` gets a
  `julia_library` named `<name>` from `src/**/*.jl`. `Project.toml` becomes
  `data`, and `[deps]` become dependencies.
- When `test/runtests.jl` exists, it also gets a `julia_test` named
  `<name>_test`.
- It leaves a `Project.toml` without a `name` alone.
- It never generates a `julia_binary`, and it ignores `ext/` and
  `[weakdeps]`.
- A third-party package needs a `# gazelle:resolve julia` line.

## Quality

Select the tools in a `julia` family in `dx.toml`:

```toml
[families.julia]
format = ["julia_format"]
lint = ["julialint"]
typecheck = ["jet"]
```

| Command | Tool | Override flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dx format` | JuliaFormatter 2.2.0 | |
| `dx lint` | the Julia VS Code linter (JuliaWorkspaces.jl 13.5.0) | `--@rules_dx//config:tool_julialint` |
| `dx typecheck` | JET 0.13.1 | `--@rules_dx//config:tool_jet` |

- The formatter and its packages are fetched only for Julia targets.
- A syntax error is reported with its line and column, and the file is never
  rewritten.
- Lint findings are named `julialint/<code>` at their line and column. The
  linter works offline and reads only the files dx passes.
- JET findings are reported at their line.

The [quality commands page](../cli/commands/quality.md) covers the
flags and family setup.

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//julia:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//julia:defs.bzl", "julia_library", "julia_binary", "julia_test")
```

### `julia_library`

```python
julia_library(name, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Thin wrapper over julia_library. entry defaults to name.jl, else src/name.jl, when srcs lists it.

### `julia_binary`

```python
julia_binary(name, *, srcs = None, main = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Thin wrapper over julia_binary. main is name.jl, else the single src.

### `julia_test`

```python
julia_test(name, *, srcs = None, main = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Thin wrapper over julia_test. main is name.jl, else the single src; under coverage it adds --code-coverage=user.

### `julia_standalone_binary`

```python
julia_standalone_binary(name, **kwargs)
```

Standalone binary from a dx julia_library that defines julia_main()::Cint.

### `julia_bench`

```python
julia_bench(name, *, srcs = None, main = None, deps = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

A julia_test run by dx bench: main calls DxBench.run_benchmarks(["name" => fn, ...]), which times each function with BenchmarkTools and writes dx-bench.json.

### `julia_doc_shard`

```python
julia_doc_shard(name, lib, module = "", package = "", **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one Julia library.

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for Julia:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `julia_format`, `julialint` |
| Ecosystems | julia |
| Manifests | `Project.toml` |
| Lockfiles | `Manifest.bazel.json` |

## Platforms

Julia builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- macOS arm64
- Windows x86_64

The [support matrix](../support-matrix.md) lists the platforms. There is
no Julia build for `windows_arm64`.

On Linux x86_64, Julia runs on a source-built `libjulia-internal` that
consumers download as the prebuilt `dx-julia-internal-linux-x86_64.so`
release asset. With that download, a Linux x86_64 target gets the
source-built library from any exec host. A source build of the library
needs a Linux exec host.

## API docs

`tools/dx docs` builds the API docs with `documenter`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

To declare a docs target yourself, load the rule behind it:

```python
load("@rules_dx//julia:defs.bzl", "julia_doc_shard")
```

`dx docs` documents every `julia_library` with no setup. It loads the library
under the pinned Julia, reads the docstrings of the exported and `public`
names through the pinned Documenter.jl 1.20.0, and writes a DocIr shard.

- The library is named after its root module.
- Its dependencies must be `julia_library` targets in the same workspace.
- To name the shard yourself, use `julia_doc_shard(name, lib, module, package)`
  from `@rules_dx//julia:defs.bzl`.
